Present Continuous for Future Arrangements in Questions
You can use the present continuous tense in interrogative form to ask about future arrangements.
What are we reading for today's lesson?
What are we studying next week?
A future arrangement is something that you plan in advance and for this reason, there is a high probability to happen.
To make a statement in the present continuous tense with a future meaning, you use the same structure; only if you want to specify the future sense you can add a time complement.

Examples:

  • The expert is analyzing data records tomorrow.
  • We are discussing about data mining the next Thursday.

In this opportunity, we are going to focus on the interrogative form.

Interrogative Form Structure:
Auxiliary verb to be in present + subject + main verb (-ing form) + time complement + ?
Examples:

• Is the expert analyzing data records tomorrow?
    Yes, he is.
    No, he is not/isn't.

  • Are we discussing about data mining the next Thursday?
    Yes, we are.
    No, we are not/ aren't.
If you want to make an information question, you need to follow this structure:
Wh question + auxiliary verb to be in present + subject + main verb (-ing form) + time complement (*exception “when”) + ?

Examples:

  • Why is the expert analyzing data records tomorrow?
  • When are we discussing about data mining?
Notice that in all these questions we are asking for future plans, not about what is happening right now.
When are we taking the exam about data mining?
Adjectives + infinitives
We can use adjectives + infinitives in some cases to express someone's feeling about something.
We are glad to see you after your surgery.
I'm very happy to see you too.
I'm really anxious to listen to your opinions and conclusions about the reading.
I'm curious to know how experts perform the process of refining data in order to obtain meaningful patterns.
Let's check first these definitions:

Adjectives:
A word that describes or modifies other word. It usually refers to physical characteristics or feelings.

For example: amazed, sad, glad, big and many others.

Infinitives:
A verb without any conjugation. You can identify it because it is always preceded by the preposition “to”.

For example: to eat, to sleep, to learn, and many others.

images.text:
Mr. Adams: Good morning, class! So, what are we reading for today's lesson?
George: Good morning, Mr. Adams! We're glad to see you after your surgery. Are you OK?
Mr. Adams: Yes, I am! Thanks for asking, I'm very happy to see you too. Also, I'm really anxious to listen to your opinions and conclusions about the reading.
George: Oh yes! It is about data mining. I read that it is a process that consists in examining existing databases when you need to find useful information.
Mr. Adams: Very good! Experts design databases for a data mining particular purpose, for example…
George: When you need to register scientific research, or even when you have to keep track of customers' account records. But Mr. Adams, I'm curious to know how experts perform the process of refining data in order to obtain meaningful patterns.

Mr. Adams: Well, first, the expert selects a set or a subset of data. Then, he classifies particular fields of interest, or what we know as variables. After that, he looks for specific patterns. One of the most common techniques to achieve this is the regression analysis technique.
George: Hmm, let me guess! It looks for variables that correlate with other variables, or that cluster similar data records, right?
Mr. Adams: Yes! Finally, the expert selects and extracts new data in a report or graph. Then, you can use it to show new information.
George: Excuse me, Mr. Adams! What are we studying next week?

Mr. Adams: Well, our next reading is about the importance of data mining.
George: Really? I already did it! I love this topic, I'm so happy to read about it. It explains that data mining plays an important role in businesses since it is helping companies to target different markets more every day, and online customers to find products in a faster way.
Mr. Adams: Exactly! Data mining of consumer information is an important application because the volume of commerce grows, and the amount of data that large systems generate, such as online bookstores and browsers increases.
George: I see..! When are we taking the exam about data mining?
Mr. Adams: Great question! You're taking it in two weeks.
